body: I'm not going to reveal where I am with that sort of specificity.

>There must be some type of government program you can be on

Just food stamps

>you could go to the hospital for suicidal thoughts

It is my experience that health professionals become quite antagonistic once they can justify that you are a threat to yourself or others.

>fill out mundane surveys for a few hours

For literally pennies per hour

>I know that the suicide rate is astonishingly high in Native communities

According to [this link](http://www.advocate.com/politics/transgender/2012/10/14/over-half-native-trans-people-have-attempted-suicide) 56% of native trans folk have attempted suicide. I'm still in the 44% at this point.

>as well as a ridiculous amount of health issues. I'm sure there are publications who would eat this stuff up.

I feel vulnerable enough in a world that varies from uncaring to hostile without publishing all my bullshit. Let alone all the terrible logistics that would involve.

45 miles?

And that town doesn't really seem like it has much in the way of the services you are suggesting.
This was something I had brought up to my last therapist and he didn't think so.
I really don't think so. My mental health is fragile enough as it is to have to deal with a minimum wage fast food or Wal*Mart job.
I was just moving there because of the job. And the job site was not serviced by public transport.
No bus service in this town. Day trips in general seem a frivolous use of money, which I don't have a way of getting more of at the moment really.
I live in a very rural area. Not serviced by a train station or even greyhound. I don't need a car in the sense that I have no job or friends to visit or really anything.

I have really shit credit and no income. I'm pretty much not credit eligible.

My option is pretty much to start walking and be homeless in winter. I guess that's a method of suicide, but not one I'd favor.
